newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FORECAST-Hungary gov sec market sees depo rate cut.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Hungary gov sec market sees depo rate cut.

text.p: Hungary's government securities yields are seen flat to slightly lower this week, with the market watching closely the central bank's deposit rates following Friday's repo rate cuts, traders said on Monday.
The repo rate reductions have strengthened expectations for cuts in the deposit rates in the near future, they added.
"A cut in the deposit rates would certainly push the yields down," said Gabor Pozsgay of Creditanstalt. "These rates hold the current interest rate levels."

The National Bank of Hungary cut four of its five repo rates for one day to one month maturities by 50 basis points (bp) on Friday, but left the six-month and 12-month deposit rates unchanged at 21 and 20.50 percent respectively.

The repo cuts have brought down secondary market discount Treasury bill yields for one-month to one-year maturities by 20 to 30 bps since Friday, but they pushed government bond -- two to seven years -- yields only slightly down, traders said.

The Budapest Interbank Offered Rates (BUBOR), calculated form the average rates of a selection of banks, and usually moving only one or two bps a day, dropped on Monday at an unprecedented pace of 0.48 bps for one month and 0.21 percent for three months.
Traders said that expectations for repo rate cuts had already been built in the yields partly before Friday but the short-term yields may go further down by a few bps this week.
However, a substantial fall would come, mainly in the case of government bonds, only if the central bank cuts its deposit rates, traders said.
They added that a cut of probably 25 bps, but perhaps as much as 50 bps, may come as soon as at the end of this week.

They said all the macroeconomic data published recently, including April CPI, preliminary April PPI and preliminary March current account and trade figures were positive and projected the further decline of inflation and interest rates.
Consumer price inflation ran at 18.6 percent in April and the government expects it to go down to between 16 to 17 percent by December.
Traders said that the yields of discount Treasury bills were likely to drop by five to 25 pips at this week's auctions, due to Friday's repo cuts.
